newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains down, shipper buying limits losses.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains down, shipper buying limits losses.

text.p: LIFFE wheat and barley futures eased on Tuesday, but they were well underpinned by shipper buying and the losses were limited, traders said.
The basic reason for lower prices was the strength of sterling against other European currencies, they said.
On wheat, active May last traded down 0.60 stg at 95.00 stg per tonne. May traded 257 lots out of 576 in total.
On barley active May last traded down 1.00 stg at 93.00 stg. There were 21 lots done on May out of a total of 48 in barley.

Shippers were brought into futures by the difficulty of getting supplies on the physical market, one trader said. "People can't get it on the physical market, so they come to futures to get cover," he said.
The trader said there had been some profit taking selling late in the day.
